name: azure-monitor
description: Monitors Azure resources with metrics and alerts: metric retrieval, alert rule creation, action groups, and activity log queries.
author: Kdesk-Catalog

capabilities.name: metrics
commands: az monitor metrics list --resource <resource-id> --metric-names Requests --start-time 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-08-01T23:59:59Z --interval PT1H
az monitor metrics list --resource <resource-id> --metric-names Requests --aggregation count --top 5
examples: az monitor metrics list --resource <resource-id> --metric-names "Requests" "5XX" --start-time $(date -u -d '1 day ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --interval PT6H
az monitor metrics list --resource <resource-id> --metric-names Percentage CPU --aggregation average

capabilities.name: alerts
commands: az monitor alert create --name api-5xx --resource-group rg --condition "percentage CPU > 90 avg 5m" --resource <resource-id>
az monitor alert show --name api-5xx -g rg
az monitor alert update --name api-5xx -g rg --condition "percentage CPU > 95 avg 5m"
az monitor alert delete --name api-5xx -g rg
examples: az monitor alert create --name api-latency --resource-group rg --condition "Avg Requests Duration > 5000 avg 5m" --resource <appinsights-id> --action <action-group-id>
az monitor alert list --resource-group rg --query '[].{name:name,severity:severity}' -o table
az monitor alert create --name vm-down --resource-group rg --condition "All VM sizes - count > 0" --resource <vm-id>

capabilities.name: activity-log
commands: az monitor activity-log list --category Administrative --query '[].{time:eventTimestamp,op:operationName.value}' -o table
examples: az monitor activity-log list --status Failed --max-events 50 | jq '.[].operationName.value'

instructions:
# Azure Monitor

## What this skill does

Monitors Azure resources: retrieving metrics over time windows, creating metric/activity alerts with conditions, managing action groups, and querying the activity log.

## When to use

- Checking an API's request count or latency trend
- Creating an alert for a new resource
- Auditing failed operations

## Real commands

```bash
# List available metrics
az monitor metrics list-definitions --resource <resource-id>

# Retrieve a metric for a day
az monitor metrics list --resource <resource-id> --metric-names Requests --start-time 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-08-01T23:59:59Z --interval PT1H

# Create an alert
az monitor alert create --name api-5xx --resource-group rg --condition "percentage CPU > 90 avg 5m" --resource <resource-id>

# List alerts
az monitor alert list --resource-group rg --query '[].{name:name,severity:severity}' -o table

# Activity log failures
az monitor activity-log list --status Failed --max-events 20
```

## Testing

- Trigger an alert condition intentionally and confirm firing state
- Verify action group notifications arrive

## Best practices

- Use App Insights queries for application-level metrics
- Aggregate alerts per resource group for manageability
- Set action groups with escalation paths
